items.stem: Which method selects rows and columns of a DataFrame by their labels?

options.rationale: Correct: .loc selects by row and column labels.
.iloc selects by integer position, not label.
.at accesses a single scalar by label, not a range of rows and columns.
.where masks values by condition; it does not select by label.

items.explanation: Correct: .loc is label-based selection for rows and columns.

items.stem: Which TWO methods handle missing values in a pandas DataFrame? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: fillna replaces missing values with a specified value or strategy.
Correct: dropna removes rows or columns containing missing values.
merge joins DataFrames by key; it does not handle missing values.
sort_values orders rows; it does not handle missing values.

items.explanation: Correct: fillna replaces and dropna removes missing values.

items.stem: Why are vectorised pandas operations usually preferred over Python for-loops over rows?

options.text: They run optimised C-level operations over whole arrays and are far faster
options.rationale: Correct: vectorised operations avoid per-row Python overhead and run in optimised compiled code.

options.text: They change the data in place to save memory
options.rationale: Vectorised operations still typically return new objects; speed is the reason.
Vectorisation does not clean data by itself.

options.text: They are the only way to add a column
options.rationale: Columns can be added in other ways; vectorisation is about performance.

items.explanation: Correct: vectorised operations process whole arrays in compiled code, avoiding slow row loops.
